67.content: Xenochromatic Creatures are special Fontemer Aberrants met underwater. They do not attack and cannot be damaged, but striking one lets a diver borrow its ability, such as a shield, water blades or a thrown hat-shaped bomb, until they leave the water.

68.content: Archenoul is a diver in Poisson, Fontaine, employed by Spina di Rosula, who says they seldom take outside commissions. They explain that people without Visions need specialised training and a professional's company on first dives, and warn about cramps and pressure-related symptoms.

69.content:
Eitr (also: Embryonic-Ichoric-Telluric-Rudiment, the Eitr): The Eitr, full name Embryonic-Ichoric-Telluric-Rudiment, is a forbidden creation of Hyperborea, the lost golden city of Snezhnaya. It contains the power of the Light Realm and can be used to alter living bodies. In 7.1 the dying Ronova fused an orb of it to Snezhnaya's Celestial Nail.

The Belyi Tsar found it in the Shadow Realm, and the Hvergelmir institute later experimented with it, most visibly on a Snegovik.

In universe: Canon describes the Eitr as the final result of forbidden technology that let Hyperborea's master crafters modify the very essence of life. It carries Light Realm power. Used on a body, it can give a creature power beyond what its kind normally has.

According to the Eye of Graeae, the Belyi Tsar obtained the Eitr not long after delving into the Shadow Realm, but began Eitr research only some time afterwards; no one knows why. A note left by a noble figure at the Pale Crown Palace records that during his 446th foray into the Shadow Realm the writer found the Eitr together with records about it. Those records concern Hyperborea's fate and its attempt to reach the original light of the world.

Known uses: Two uses are shown in canon. First, experimentation on living beings: the Snegovik Donskoy was turned into a snow giant by the Eitr (World Quest "A Great Heart Fettered by Slender Chains", 7.0), and the hidden objective "A Certain Noble's Relics" has the Traveler fight a Snegovik described as Eitr-altered and bound in ice. Second, Ronova's final act (see the 7.1 section below).

Limits: Do not turn the Eitr into a generic power-up or an item anyone can carry. Canon shows it only in Hyperborean and Hvergelmir research and in Ronova's hands, and it is tied to forbidden knowledge and Light Realm power. Its mechanism is unexplained.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): treat the Eitr as something spoken of in hushed, uneasy terms, if at all. Hvergelmir records, old researchers and the Eye of Graeae are natural sources. Ordinary Snezhnayans would not know the name.

70.comment: Eitr: Ronova's fusion of the Eitr
70.content: In "Black Feathers Scattered at Parting" (7.1), Ronova fused the Eitr to Snezhnaya's Celestial Nail as she died. She spoke of making Teyvat feel what dying is like as the Holy Soil spreads. Afterwards, pillars of light loomed over the six Nails.

71.content: Hvergelmir, the old research institute, held the Eitr after the Belyi Tsar found it. Koshchei and Pavlina used it in experiments on living beings. Pavlina, the Snegovik princess, modified Snegovik with it; Donskoy is the best-known subject.

72.content: Donskoy was a Snegovik transformed into a snow giant by the Eitr. In the 7.0 World Quest "A Great Heart Fettered by Slender Chains" a gentle voice says his spirit was damaged during the war and that Pavlina ordered that a human girl not be allowed to meet him; Pavlina's own voice says he needs long, peaceful sleep. His own entry carries the rest.

73.content:
Electro (also: Electro element, element of lightning): Electro is the element of lightning, one of Teyvat's seven elements. Its Archon is Beelzebul, publicly the Raiden Shogun, the God of Eternity who rules Inazuma, the land of thunder. Electro Vision holders conjure sparks, bolts and charged storms, and Electro reacts with every other element but itself. As of 7.1 the Electro Gnosis is no longer with the Archon: it passed through several hands and now belongs to the Tsaritsa.

The people of Inazuma associate Electro with their god, with storms and with the Shogunate. Vajrada Amethyst is the ascension gem of Electro characters, named after the vajra, a thunderbolt weapon of Indra.

In universe: Most people cannot use Electro. Those who can usually hold an Electro Vision. The current Electro Archon, Ei, draws on the Electro Authority of her divine throne in Celestia; she no longer holds the Electro Gnosis.

Electro appears in nature as lightning during a thunderstorm. Lightning can strike a person or the body of water they stand in.

Archon and nation: Archon: Ei, whose divine name is Beelzebul, the God of Eternity, publicly known as the Raiden Shogun. "Baal", the divine name of her late twin Makoto, and the title Raiden Shogun were long understood to refer to both twins. Nation: Inazuma, ruled by the Inazuma Shogunate.

Ei is the second holder of the title; the first was her twin Makoto, who died in the cataclysm 500 years ago. About 400 years ago Ei built the Shogun, a puppet in her image that governs Inazuma, and placed her own mind in the Plane of Euthymia, sealed inside the sword Musou Isshin. Most Inazumans do not know the Shogun is a puppet or that Makoto existed.

Gnosis and authority: Ei gave the Electro Gnosis to Yae Miko about 400 years ago, before retreating into the Plane of Euthymia. She remains the Electro Archon without it.

Vision hunt note: For about a year before the Traveler reached Inazuma, no new Electro Visions appeared. Ei was surprised to hear of it, so the cause remains unknown.

Elemental beings: Electro elemental lifeforms such as Electro Slimes, Electro Specters and the Electro Hypostasis, and the Thunder Manifestation of Amakumo Peak.

Electro Slimes form from Electro coalescing in nature. Electro Specters are born of highly concentrated Electro and float. The Electro Hypostasis (code name Aleph) is a high-purity Electro entity at Cape Oath in Mondstadt. The Electro Regisvine of Sumeru's Lokapala Jungle is a giant plant that releases charge stored in the ley lines.

Known uses: Lightning strikes, sparks that chain between foes, charged fields, and fast bursts of speed. Electro also sets off reactions with Pyro, Hydro, Cryo, Anemo, Geo and Dendro.

Electro also drives devices in Inazuma: Lightning Strike Probes respond to anyone affected by Electro.

Limits: Electro does not react with itself. It has no effect of its own beyond enabling reactions.

Electro on its own does not change the target; it only enables reactions. A Vision fixes its holder to one element: Kazuha's brief Electro use came from a second Vision.

Interactions: Overloaded (with Pyro) explodes. Superconduct (with Cryo) damages and weakens Physical resistance. Electro-Charged (with Hydro) damages over time. Swirl spreads Electro. Crystallize with Geo forms a shield-granting shard. Quicken with Dendro enables Aggravate and Spread.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): Electro is a damage type and the element of characters such as Fischl, Keqing, Raiden Shogun, Yae Miko, Cyno, Flins and Ineffa. Its ascension gems are Vajrada Amethyst.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): show Electro as light, sound and sudden force: a bright flash, a crack and rumble, hair lifting from static, the metallic smell of a storm. Violet is the usual colour cue, matching the Vajrada Amethyst and the Thunderbird's purple thunder; the wiki notes Electro can occasionally be seen as yellow. Keep scale proportionate: a Vision holder can arc sparks, not summon a storm.

74.content: The Electro Archon is the God of Eternity among the Seven and ruler of Inazuma. There have been two holders: Raiden Makoto, who died in the cataclysm 500 years ago, and her twin sister Ei, who succeeded her and has held the Electro Authority since. The Shogun puppet, built in the twins' image, is now the public face of the Archon. Titles such as "Raiden Shogun", "Narukami" and "Electro Archon" in older texts may refer to any of the three or to the general idea of Inazuma's god.

75.content: The Electro Gnosis was Ei's, entrusted to Yae Miko about 400 years ago, then traded to Scaramouche for the Traveler's safety, taken by Nahida in Sumeru, handed to Dottore, and now belongs to the Tsaritsa along with five other Gnoses (as of 7.1). No one outside the Archon can easily use it: Scaramouche could, but only with heavy modification, and Nahida could not use it in battle.

76.content: Kapatcir ("Great Eagle of the Storm") was a monster, a huge violet bird of prey in storm and thunder, worshipped as a guardian by the tribe of Tsurumi Island. The boy Ruu named her; when the tribe sacrificed him, she destroyed the mountain in grief and rage, killing the tribe, and left a curse on the land. Years later Ei hunted her down as "an obstacle to progress" and sealed the remnants of her power at the Asase Shrine on Seirai Island. A thousand years on, Hibiki's release of that seal let the Thunder Manifestation loose.

77.content: Electro Visions are the external apparatuses by which people wield lightning. No new Electro Visions appeared for about a year before the Traveler reached Inazuma, and the reason is unknown. Many were taken by the Vision Hunt Decree and returned once it was rescinded. Known Electro Vision holders include Keqing, Fischl, Beidou, Razor, Kazuha's late friend and, 500 years ago, Fukami.

78.content: Electroculi are consolidated Electro energy scattered across Inazuma. Item text describes them as a substance that "has accumulated intense Electro energy", offered at a Statue of The Seven to help it regain lost power. The wiki counts 181 in the overworld.

79.content:
Electro-Charged (also: Electro-Charged reaction, Electrocharged, Electro Charged): Electro-Charged is what happens when Electro and Hydro meet on a target, in either order. The target keeps both Hydro and Electro on it and takes Electro damage once a second, and the shock jumps to another wet enemy nearby. It continues until one of the two elements is used up.

The wiki lists it as a Transformative reaction. A third element can still react with the target, which makes Electro-Charged a good opener for follow-up reactions.

In universe: Canon offers no in-world explanation. Electro-Charged appears in tutorials and combat, not in character dialogue in the sources read. Treat it as a gameplay abstraction that a scene may borrow from.

The in-game tutorial puts it plainly: Electro meeting Hydro causes Electro-Charged, which keeps dealing Electro damage until it wears off and electrifies nearby Wet opponents.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): Electro-Charged leaves the target with a Hydro aura and an Electro aura at the same time. It deals Electro damage once per second; each tick reduces both auras by 0.4 gauge units, and it ends when either aura is gone. Normal aura decay still applies.

- It cannot damage off-field characters. Switching away pauses the ticks; if the character returns while still affected by Electro and Hydro, the ticks resume.
- Each time it deals damage it also hits one other nearby Wet opponent, about 5 m away (the wiki marks that range as unverified), accounting for that opponent's Electro RES. The Wet aura is not consumed by the arc, and an Electro aura is not applied to the arc target.
- If Electro-Charged ends because an aura expires, one more tick can occur if more than 0.5 seconds have passed since the last.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): show Electro-Charged as lightning crawling over wet surfaces: blue-white arcs skittering across a soaked body, a crackle in the air, hair and cloth standing up. The shock should leap between soaked enemies and puddles.

Examples: A Hydro slime drenches a group of enemies, then a bolt of lightning strikes one of them. The charge crackles along its wet body and jumps to another soaked enemy a few steps away, repeating until the water or the lightning fades.

Limits: It needs Electro and Hydro together: Anemo, Geo, Pyro, Cryo and Dendro do not cause it. Do not describe it as an instant burst; its identity is the sustained shock. Do not have it hit off-field targets, or spread to dry ones, as the wiki shows it arcs only to Wet opponents.

80.content:
Elemental Burst (also: Ultimate, character ultimate): The Elemental Burst, or Burst, is a Talent that needs Energy and is usually stronger than the Elemental Skill. Fans call it the ultimate, or "Q" after its default PC key. Every character has one unlocked from the start. This is a gameplay mechanic; the narrative equivalent is a character unleashing their strongest technique.

Casting grants a character a few seconds of invincibility frames (the exact time varies per character), during which the HP bar is locked and no damage from enemies or debuffs is taken.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): a Burst can be used when (1) it is off cooldown and (2) the character holds at least the Burst's Energy Cost. Energy beyond the cost is ignored. Using it spends all Energy and starts a short cooldown, though Energy can still be gathered during the cooldown.

- Readiness: the HUD icon glows with an audio cue; off-field characters show a ready icon beside their portrait, and co-op players show a marker beside their names.
- Typical costs and cooldowns: 40 Energy with a 12 s cooldown; 50 with 13.5 s; 60 with 15 s; 70 with 18 s; 80 with 20 s; 90 with 18 s or 22 s.
- Exceptions: Hour of Burning Skies and Havoc: Ruin do not use Energy. The first spends Fighting Spirit (100-200) gathered from the party's Normal Attacks and Nightsoul point use in combat. The second uses Skirk's Serpent's Subtlety points (50-100) and has a 15 s cooldown.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): present a Burst as a character's signature, high-effort moment, a surge of power they can only call on after the fight has built momentum. Avoid quoting Energy costs or cooldowns in character. Match the character's element and weapon in the description.

Limits: The Energy meter, key binding and cooldown are interface concepts, not things characters mention.

Figures are those listed on the wiki as of 7.1.

81.content:
Elemental Mastery: Elemental Mastery is an attribute that enhances elemental reactions. The higher it is, the stronger the reactions a character triggers. It is a gameplay stat with no direct in-world number.

Most playable characters start at 0. The exceptions are Lauma and Nefer, who begin at 200 and 100 respectively. It has existed since version 1.0.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): on triggering a reaction, Elemental Mastery boosts it. Overloaded, Superconduct, Electro-Charged, Burning, Shattered, Swirl, Bloom, Hyperbloom, Burgeon, Lunar-Charged, Lunar-Bloom, Lunar-Crystallize and Stellar-Conduct deal more damage. Melt and Vaporize multiply the triggering attack. Aggravate and Spread add bonus base damage to the triggering attack. Crystallize shields absorb more damage.

Bonus is computed as a percentage that grows with diminishing returns: the formulas are 2.78 x EM / (EM + 1400) for Vaporize and Melt, 16 x EM / (EM + 2000) for the transformative reactions listed above, 5 x EM / (EM + 1200) for Aggravate and Spread, 6 x EM / (EM + 2000) for the Lunar reactions and Stellar-Conduct, and 4.44 x EM / (EM + 1400) for Crystallize shields. The bonus is added to the reaction bonus in a multiplier of 1 + EM bonus + reaction bonus. Every extra point of mastery gives less than the last.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): a character with a lot of mastery is deft at combining elements and can make reactions blossom larger; show it through precision, timing and a feel for how elements push on each other rather than numbers. Characters tied to reactions in the story, such as Sucrose and Alhaitham, suit this portrayal, but their stat values are not canon facts.

Limits: No canon defines the stat outside the game's interface and tutorial text.

The attribute does not change Vision type or the elements a person can use.

82.content:
Elemental Reaction (also: Elemental Reactions, elemental aura, Transformative Reaction, Amplifying Reaction, Additive Reaction): An Elemental Reaction happens when an element is applied to a target that already carries a different element. Attacks, Visions and elemental creatures leave an "aura" of their element on a target, and a second element meeting it triggers an effect such as Vaporize, Melt, Overloaded, Swirl, Bloom or Crystallize. It is chiefly a combat rule, so treat it as a gameplay abstraction that a scene may borrow from, not as a named in-world law.

Reactions fall into groups by how they work: Transformative reactions deal their own damage, Amplifying reactions multiply the hit that triggered them, and Additive reactions add to it. Two newer families sit on top of these: Lunar reactions (from the Hydro-related reactions) and Stellar Glimmer reactions (from the Cryo-related ones).

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): when an element is applied to an enemy, player or object it leaves an aura that fades over time. Applying a second, different element triggers a reaction, which consumes some or all of the first aura. Many attack sources have an internal cooldown, so they cannot reapply their element, or trigger a reaction, on every hit.

The base reactions by element pair, as listed on the wiki's overview table:
- Pyro with Hydro: Vaporize. Pyro with Electro: Overloaded. Pyro with Cryo: Melt. Pyro with Dendro: Burning.
- Hydro with Electro: Electro-Charged. Hydro with Cryo: Frozen (a frozen target hit by Geo or a blunt Physical attack Shatters). Hydro with Dendro: Bloom.
- Electro with Cryo: Superconduct. Electro with Dendro: Quicken.
- Anemo with Pyro, Hydro, Electro or Cryo: Swirl. Geo with Pyro, Hydro, Electro or Cryo: Crystallize.
- Bloom can follow with Pyro as Burgeon or with Electro as Hyperbloom; Quicken can follow with Dendro as Spread or with Electro as Aggravate.
- Dendro with Cryo, and Dendro with Anemo or Geo, do not react. Geo cannot be the first element on a target, so it only ever reacts as the second.

Lunar reactions: Lunar reactions are a subset of reactions. To trigger one, the party must include a character with a Moonsign Benediction passive talent that converts specific Hydro-related reactions. There are three: Lunar-Charged (Electro with Hydro), Lunar-Bloom (Dendro with Hydro) and Lunar-Crystallize (Geo with Hydro). Unlike their base versions, Lunar reactions can CRIT.

Stellar glimmer reactions: Stellar Glimmer reactions are a subset of reactions, triggered when a party includes a character with a passive talent that converts specific Cryo-related reactions. There are two: Stellar-Conduct (Cryo with Electro) and Stellar Swirl (Anemo with Cryo). They also interrupt a specific attack of Snowland Fae and Aberrant Chimeric Monsters.

In universe: Canon discussion of reactions is thin: most of the system is delivered as tutorial text and combat feedback. The pages read offer one clear in-world statement, that Stellar Glimmer reactions were brought to ancient Snezhnaya by Saarelainen. Stellar Linchpin users are described in quest material as having power that appears to come from beyond Teyvat, and the Snezhnayan reactions are enabled by their Stellar Jubilee passives.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): describe reactions as visible, sensible results of two elements colliding. Fire on water becomes a burst of steam, fire on ice a fast melt, lightning in water a crackling spread, wind carrying flame, frost or sparks outward, stone crystallising around an element. Keep the effects local to the people involved.

Limits: Do not treat the tables above as cosmic law. Dendro does not react with Cryo, Anemo or Geo, and Physical damage reacts only as the Shatter follow-up to Frozen. Do not credit a reaction to the wrong trigger: a reaction counts for the character that triggers it, not the one who left the first aura.

83.content: Transformative reactions deal their own instance of damage, separate from the hit that caused them: Overloaded, Shattered, Electro-Charged, Superconduct, Swirl, Burning, Bloom, Hyperbloom and Burgeon. Their damage depends on reaction type, the triggering character's level and Elemental Mastery; it cannot CRIT.

84.content: Vaporize and Melt multiply the damage of the attack that triggers them. The stronger "forward" case is 2x (Hydro onto Pyro, Pyro onto Cryo), the weaker "reverse" 1.5x (Pyro onto Hydro, Cryo onto Pyro), and the weaker case tends to leave more of the first element in place.

85.content: Spread and Aggravate, the follow-ups to Quicken, add a flat bonus to the base damage of the triggering hit. The name "Additive Reactions" is unofficial; the game's Miliastra Wonderland mode calls them "Catalyze Reactions".

86.content: An aura is the lasting mark of an element on a target. It decays over time, and triggering a reaction shortens or removes it by an amount that depends on the reaction and the strength of the second element.

87.content:
Elemental Resonance (also: Team Bonus, party resonance): Elemental Resonance is a game bonus granted when a full party contains certain element combinations. Two or more characters of the same element among the first four party slots trigger that element's resonance. Four different elements trigger Protective Canopy. It is a gameplay mechanic, not an in-world phenomenon.

Resonances depend only on the first four party members, work in Co-Op Mode, and do not need all members alive. A third or fourth character of the same element adds nothing more.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore), as of 7.1:
- Fervent Flames (two Pyro): 40% shorter Cryo effect, ATK +25%.
- Soothing Water (two Hydro): 40% shorter Pyro effect, Max HP +25%.
- High Voltage (two Electro): 40% shorter Hydro effect; certain Electro reactions have a 100% chance to produce an Electro particle (5 s cooldown).
- Shattering Ice (two Cryo): 40% shorter Electro effect, CRIT Rate +15% against Frozen or Cryo-affected enemies.
- Impetuous Winds (two Anemo): stamina use -15%, movement speed +10%, skill cooldowns -5%.
- Enduring Rock (two Geo): shield strength +15%, plus damage and Geo RES reduction effects when shields or Moondrifts are nearby.
- Sprawling Greenery (two Dendro): Elemental Mastery +50 and reaction-triggered boosts.
- Protective Canopy (four unique elements): all Elemental RES +15% and Physical RES +15%.

- Enduring Rock details: when a shielded character or Moondrifts from Lunar-Crystallize are nearby, damage dealt rises 15%, and dealing damage lowers enemy Geo RES by 20% for 15 s.
- Sprawling Greenery details: after Burning, Quicken, Bloom or Lunar-Bloom, nearby party members gain 30 Elemental Mastery for 6 s; after Aggravate, Spread, Hyperbloom or Burgeon, they gain 20 for 6 s. The durations count independently.
- High Voltage triggers: Superconduct, Stellar-Conduct, Overloaded, Electro-Charged, Lunar-Charged, Quicken, Aggravate or Hyperbloom.
- Co-op rule: if some of a co-op party is inside a Domain, only the characters in the Domain determine resonance and benefit from it.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): represent a resonance as companions who work especially well together, such as two Pyro users feeding each other's flames, with a visible shared glow of their element. Do not quote percentages in character. Protective Canopy can be shown as a diverse team covering one another's weaknesses.

Limits: Only a full party triggers resonance, except that Protective Canopy needs four unique elements. Extra same-element characters add nothing.

Unlisted: this entry does not cover individual talents or weapons that depend on the party's elements.

88.content: Protective Canopy is the resonance granted by a party of four unique elements: all Elemental RES +15% and Physical RES +15%.

89.content:
Elemental Sight (also: elemental trails, elemental traces): Elemental Sight is the ability to perceive the elements around you. Toggling it makes elemental traces visible, shows which nearby things are affected by an element and highlights what can be interacted with. In Teyvat it is bound up with owning a Vision, or at least having elemental sensitivity, which is rare but known.

The Traveler is among those canon confirms to have it, and the wiki also lists Amber, Lisa, Rosaria and Yanfei.

In universe: Elemental traces, also called elemental trails, are left behind by almost anything elemental, from slimes to gods to the wind itself, and can also be left by elemental magic or Vision holders. Everyone knows they exist, but those without elemental affinity find them hard to sense.

Sensitivity varies even between people who can wield the elements, and it can be trained. Lisa says she heard the Traveler's sensitivity is very strong, and later only calls a drawing clear once the Traveler has copied what they saw with Elemental Sight. Bennett is implied to have weak sensitivity: he wanted to swap his goggles for "Alchemist's Goggles", an item rumoured to let anyone see even the faintest elemental energy. Timaeus dismissed those goggles as impossible. An allogene who gives up their Vision may stay sensitive, as Jiangxue does.

Gameplay: Gameplay: Elemental Sight is toggled with a button beside the minimap (middle mouse button by default on PC). A white range indicator spreads from the active character; background objects turn dark and muted while interactable ones are highlighted.

It shows elemental trails for bounties, between Seelie and their gardens, between Monetoo and their resting places and in certain quests and hidden exploration objectives, and it shows possible routes between a Phase Gate and the gates it connects to. It also shows the element affecting enemies and most interactable objects, and reveals enemy name tags. Highlight colours follow the element: white for nothing, red for fire, torches and explosive barrels, blue for things made Wet, light blue for recently deactivated flamethrowers and Mist Flowers, purple for unbroken Electro crystals, yellow for Geo constructs and ore, turquoise for Anemo ambers and green for Dendro vines and flammable plant matter.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay (this project's interpretation, not canon): treat it as a sense, not a menu. A Vision holder can say they feel or see lingering elemental traces, noticing a trail, an enchanted thing or a hidden mechanism, but should not talk about toggles, cooldowns or colour codes. Characters without a Vision or elemental affinity should not perceive traces.

Limits: Canon gives no rule for how far elemental senses reach, and does not say that every Vision holder perceives the same things. Do not assume that all allogenes see equally well, or that people without a Vision cannot sense strong elements at all.

90.content:
Elemental Skill (also: Skill): The Elemental Skill, or just Skill, is a Talent every playable character has from the start. It costs no Energy; instead it goes on cooldown after use. It deals Elemental DMG, never Physical, and usually produces elemental particles that recharge the party's Energy.

It is the everyday counterpart of the Elemental Burst, which needs full Energy.

In universe: This is a gameplay category. In the world, the skill is simply what a character does with their element or training, such as a technique, a summoned construct or a stance. The game fixes one such signature move per character.

Gameplay: Gameplay: using the Skill starts a cooldown whose length differs per character and which cannot be used again until it ends. Cooldown can be shortened, reset or extended by Talents, Constellations and other effects.

Some skills accept more than one input before the cooldown begins, such as Diluc's and Fischl's, and they differ in whether the cooldown starts at once or after the effect expires. Single-input skills, including held ones, start cooldown straight away, with held skills starting it after the hold ends. Some skills have several Charges, shown as small squares on the icon. Many have different tap and hold versions; the hold is usually stronger but has a longer cooldown. Most Skills generate Energy particles when they damage an enemy.

Limits: The Skill is not the same as the Elemental Burst or as a Normal Attack. It is a game category, so characters do not name it in dialogue.

91.content:
Element (also: the Elements, the seven Elements, seven elements, elemental power, elemental Authority, elemental Authorities): The Elements are Teyvat's seven forms of elemental power: Anemo (wind), Geo (earth), Electro (lightning), Dendro (plants), Hydro (water), Pyro (fire) and Cryo (ice). Each is bound to one Archon and that Archon's nation. Ordinary people wield an element through a Vision, a jewel-like focus granted to those with strong desires.

Behind the modern order lie the Seven Sovereigns, the elemental dragons of the old world, whose Authorities were taken by the Heavenly Principles and tied to the Archons' divine thrones. Archons can use their element without a Gnosis, while mortals normally need a Vision.

In universe: Each element pairs with one Archon and one nation. Canon does not explain why.

Canon does not say how an Archon relates to their element, nor how a region is shaped by its element.

The seven elements: Anemo: Mondstadt, Barbatos (Venti). Geo: Liyue, Morax (Zhongli). Electro: Inazuma, the Raiden Shogun (Ei). Dendro: Sumeru, Nahida. Hydro: Fontaine, Focalors. Pyro: Natlan, Mavuika. Cryo: Snezhnaya, the Tsaritsa (Anastasya).

Barbatos and Morax are the only two original Archons still living; the rest of the original Seven have died and been replaced. After the Cataclysm 500 years ago, Ei replaced Makoto, Nahida replaced Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, Focalors replaced Egeria, and Anastasya replaced the Belyi Tsar as Cryo Archon. Mavuika placed her life in the Sacred Flame so that she could return after 500 years.

Origins: The seven elemental Authorities were originally wielded by the Seven Sovereigns, the most powerful dragons of the old world, who ruled alongside the Dragon King Nibelung. When the Heavenly Principles came to Teyvat they took part of those Authorities and later tied them to the Divine Thrones, which became the Archons' Authorities (Calamitous Tread, 4.1). Visions are also derived from these Authorities.

Gnoses: A Gnosis is a chess-piece-like focus that, according to Venti in Ending Note (Prologue, 1.0), resonates directly with Celestia and is far more advanced than a Vision. Seven were made, one per element, and each belongs to an Archon. Archons can use their element without a Gnosis, and an Archon's divine throne exists independently of whether they hold it.

Visions: A Vision is a jewel-like amulet that lets its wearer channel one element directly. Visions are given to "allogenes", people with strong desires and the potential to become gods, and take the shape of a gem with the element's symbol, often in a regional setting. A Vision does not grant instant mastery: using the element takes practice, so skill varies widely. Visions can be channeled through mundane objects and put to everyday tasks. Those who hold one have some sensitivity to elemental energy (Elemental Sight). When a holder dies, their Vision becomes a Masterless Vision, losing its power and element indicator, though some later resonate with a new person.

Non vision sources: Not every character draws on a Vision. The Element page notes: the Traveler and the Wonderland Manekin have none; Venti, Zhongli, the Raiden Shogun, Nahida and Mavuika draw on a Gnosis or Archon power; Neuvillette on an Ancient Dragon's Authority; Skirk on the Seven-Shifting Serpent; Columbina on the Tri-Lunar Convergence.

Reactions: When a second element is applied to a target already carrying one, the two can react, for example Vaporize (Pyro with Hydro), Melt (Pyro with Cryo), Overloaded (Pyro with Electro) or Swirl (Anemo spreading another element).

Further examples: Hydro and Electro trigger Electro-Charged; Electro and Cryo, Superconduct; Hydro and Cryo freeze the target; Dendro with Hydro, Bloom; Geo produces Crystallize.

Gameplay: Gameplay, not literal lore: the Elements are seven of the eight damage types, the eighth being Physical. Each character has one element, shown by a Vision-style icon.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): treat the element as the colour and texture of a power, not a switch that controls the world. Show it through sensory cues: pressure and sound for Anemo, tremors and stone for Geo, crackle and static for Electro, growth and spores for Dendro, flow and chill for Hydro, heat and light for Pyro, frost and silence for Cryo.

Limits: A Vision fixes its holder to one element and cannot ordinarily be destroyed or tampered with by human methods. Elemental energy can run out: a Vision holder can burn through too much at once and need rest. Masterless Visions go dull when their holder dies. Gnoses held by non-owners may be restricted in what they can do.

92.content: The Seven Sovereigns are the seven most powerful elemental lifeforms of the Light Realm and ruled the old world alongside Nibelung. The Heavenly Principles took their Authorities and gave them to the Archons' thrones. Living Sovereigns cannot use their full power until their Authority is returned. The Sovereign dragons are Dvalin (Anemo), Azhdaha (Geo), Apep (Dendro), Neuvillette (Hydro) and Xiuhcoatl (Pyro).

93.content: "Allogenes" is the gods' secret term for Vision holders: people with strong desires who could one day ascend to Celestia and become gods. Venti told the Traveler this in Ending Note (Prologue). Most holders and ordinary Teyvatians do not know the word.

94.content: When a Vision's holder dies, it loses its power and element and becomes a Masterless Vision. Sometimes one resonates with a new person. The very rich seek them as commodities, according to Ningguang's account. Kaedehara Kazuha once briefly used a late friend's Masterless Electro Vision.

95.content: Moon Wheels are Vision-like objects associated with Nod-Krai and the moon, formed from the stuff of the soul in a pact between the Heavenly Principles and the Moon Sisters. They use kuuvahki, an older, purer elemental power, and enable Lunar Reactions in combat. Nod-Krai Moon Wheels look identical to Nod-Krai Visions; Zibai, the only Moon Wheel user from outside Nod-Krai, has a differently shaped frame.

96.content: Stellar Linchpins are Vision-like objects from Snezhnaya, whose users have a power that seems to come from beyond Teyvat. Fatui research links them to the dead Third Descender, Saarelainen: impurities from its remains fix in place when a Linchpin manifests. Known users include Sandrone, Odette and Vesna; they enable Stellar Glimmer Reactions.

97.content:
Energy (also: Elemental Energy, Energy Recharge, elemental particles, elemental orbs): Energy is the resource a character spends on their Elemental Burst. It builds up from elemental particles and orbs, which drop when Elemental Skills hit enemies or when enemies lose HP, and which recharge the whole party. Using the Burst empties it.

Characters with special energy, such as Mavuika and Skirk, work differently and are mostly outside the rules below.

In universe: Characters do not speak of Energy as a number. The nearest in-world idea is elemental energy: pulses of an element a fighter gathers and then releases in a signature technique. Canon lore elsewhere says elemental energy was made by the Heavenly Principles, who divided raw currents of the Light Realm into seven using Phlogiston as a base (revealed 5.1).

Treat the particles as flecks of an element shed in a fight and drawn to the character, which fits how they glow and fly toward a fighter.

Gameplay: Gameplay: each Burst has its own Energy cost, and a character cannot hold more than their base Burst needs. Being knocked out removes all of a character's Energy; if the active character falls out of bounds or drowns, the whole team loses all Energy.

Particles and orbs recharge the entire party, but only when they reach a character. Energy gained depends on element match, Energy Recharge, whether the character is active and party size. Per particle at 100 percent Energy Recharge, an active character gets 3 from a particle of their own element, 1 of a different element and 2 if non-elemental; orbs give three times as much. Inactive characters get 60 percent of the active rate with four in the party, 70 percent with three and 80 percent with two.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay (this project's interpretation, not canon): describe a character building toward a signature technique as they fight, gathering momentum from elemental flecks, and releasing it all at once. Do not quote numbers or conversion rates in character.

Limits: Gameplay figures in this entry are mechanics, not world facts. Canon has no in-world rule that a hit produces a set amount of energy, nor a "party" that pools it.

98.content:
Exorcism (also: exorcist arts, Liyue thaumaturgy, thaumaturgy, thaumaturge, thaumaturges): Exorcists, also called thaumaturges, are Liyue people who have sworn an oath to cleanse the land of ghosts, spirits and demons. They are skilled in combat, magic and martial arts, and most come from families that keep exorcism as the family trade.

Canon names few groups: the Tianheng Thaumaturges (Chongyun's clan), the family of Yelan and the Lan Clan. This entry covers the tradition; the Exorcists culture entry covers the people.

In universe: Chongyun's clan motto, as recorded in his and Shenhe's voice-overs, is to keep the heart pure and evil erased. The Tianheng clan keeps handed-down books recording the spirits it has defeated.

Little is known of origins. The wiki says Liyue thaumaturgy took its modern form around 500 years ago after the Cataclysm, when a revolution in weapon and catalyst making shifted favour toward supernatural arts over traditional martial arts, though thaumaturges still practise both. Exorcist arts seem close to adeptal arts: Chongyun counts Shenhe, who trained under the adepti, as a master exorcist.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): exorcists favour talismans, wards, mantras and dedicated discipline over spectacle. A clan trade means family loyalty and inherited books and relics. They are not equal to adepti or Archons.

99.content:
Fetor (also: fetor of death, Fetor Node, death energy): Fetor is the energy that leaks into the living world when the border between life and death is disturbed. It is a sign of death pressing in on the living and harms those it touches. It was revealed in the limited-time Liyue event "Springtime Charms" (Lantern Rite, 5.3).

Canon says it is not Abyssal and not divine in origin, and Chongyun distinguishes it from the "evil spirits" exorcists hunt.

In universe: Small leaks happen whenever the border is disturbed. The Wangsheng Funeral Parlor is responsible for burning them away with its secret technique, the Art of Homa. In the event, Chongyun senses a strange chill around a dying elder and names it the "fetor of death."

The body absorbs fetor easily and, like Abyssal energy, it seems to linger. In humans it sharply speeds up ageing, leading to fatigue, weakness, coma and eventually death. In monsters such as hilichurls it drives a frenzy. Adepti such as Xiao can perceive it directly; ordinary people mostly cannot, though they may feel unnaturally cold near it. Xiao can share his perception by marking a person with a Witness Sigil.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): during the event, fetor appears as balls of dark energy and as Fetor Nodes that can be temporarily dispelled with physical attacks.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): show fetor through cold, a heavy hush, tired limbs and people who look suddenly older. Only adepti and those marked by one see it clearly. Keep it Liyue-specific and distinct from Abyssal taint, curses and ghosts.

100.content: Fetor can accumulate into Fetor Nodes. In the Springtime Charms event they are dispelled for a time by physical attacks, which opens the way past them.

101.content:
Frozen (also: Frozen reaction, Freeze Aura, Hydro-Cryo reaction): Frozen is the elemental reaction that happens when Hydro and Cryo meet on a target, in either order. It deals no damage by itself. It encases the target in ice and holds it immobile for a short time. A heavy blunt blow or a Geo attack can then break the ice open, which is the Shatter follow-up. It is a combat rule, so treat it as a gameplay abstraction that a scene may borrow from.

Frozen has been part of the game since Version 1.0. The in-game tutorial says to wet opponents with Hydro, then switch to a Cryo character to trigger Frozen and control them. Shatter has its own id, system.shattered, and is also described briefly here.

In universe: Canon does not give a story explanation for Frozen. The in-game text is a plain tutorial: when Cryo meets Hydro the Frozen reaction is triggered, and frozen beings cannot move.

Nothing in the sources read ties the reaction to a named character, god or event. Do not invent an origin, for example a Cryo Archon's spell or a Fatui technique.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): Frozen needs Hydro applied to a target already carrying Cryo, or Cryo applied to a target carrying Hydro. It deals no damage of its own. It gives the target a Freeze Aura that immobilises it for a while.

- The Freeze Aura's duration depends on the smaller of the two elemental amounts involved (the wiki's gauge units), and a target with Freeze Resistance stays frozen for less time.
- Shatter is triggered when a Frozen target is hit by a blunt attack or by Geo. It deals Physical damage and removes the Freeze Aura.
- Applying Pyro to a Freeze Aura consumes it and triggers Melt, Electro triggers Superconduct, and Anemo triggers Swirl.
- A blunt hit first uses up part of the Freeze Aura according to its Poise damage, and Shatter occurs only if some Freeze Aura is left afterwards.

Environment: Gameplay: in the open world, parts of most bodies of water can be frozen by Cryo attacks, and characters and enemies can stand on the ice. Pyro melts the ice instantly, and Electro on it can cause Superconduct, which the wiki notes also happens near Electro-Charged water.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): show Frozen as a visible shell of ice that forms fast around the target, with a sharp crack and a spray of fragments when it breaks. A frozen person or creature is held in place, not killed; keep it a short, temporary combat effect. Frost is the Cryo cue; a blow that cracks the ice should feel heavy, like a hammer or a stone-hard Geo strike.

Limits: Frozen does not hurt by itself, and it does not last long. It does not work on every enemy.

The Freeze Aura does not react with Hydro. Elemental shields and some innate enemy auras carry a different frozen state of Cryo that is not the same as a reaction-made Freeze Aura.

Examples: Gameplay example, from the in-game tutorial: soak an opponent with Hydro, then switch to a Cryo character and attack, and the opponent is frozen. A hammer strike or a Geo blow then Shatters it.

102.content: Shatter is the follow-up to Frozen. When a Frozen target is hit by a blunt attack or a Geo attack, the ice breaks and the target takes Physical damage; the Freeze Aura is removed. It uses the transformative-reaction damage model. Its own entry is system.shattered. The wiki's main page for it redirects to the Frozen page.

103.content:
Geo (also: Geo element, element of earth, element of rock, element of stone): Geo is the element of earth and stone, one of Teyvat's seven elements, seen in stone constructs, crystal shields and shaking ground. Its Archon is Morax (Rex Lapis), God of Contracts, patron of Liyue. He staged his own "death", gave up his Gnosis and now lives as Zhongli in Liyue Harbor.

Neuvillette addresses the Geo Archon as Deus Auri. Geo ascension gems are Prithiva Topaz.

In universe: Few people can use Geo, usually through a Geo Vision. Morax draws on the Geo Authority of his divine throne in Celestia instead; the Geo "Vision" at Zhongli's back is not a real one.

Geo's gifts to people are practical. A Liyue legend credits the Lord of Rock with the first settlers' stone stoves and struck-stone fires, which is why taverns once worshipped him as "God of the Stove"; the Moonlight Merriment event later shows that legend is false, as the true God of the Stove was Marchosius (now Guoba), whose tales merged into Morax's over time. Legend credits Rex Lapis with raising Mt. Tianheng and imprisoning the sea god Osial under the stone lances now called the Guyun Stone Forest. The Geo Archon's power was also what minted Mora, the currency of all Teyvat, at the Golden House.

Archon and nation: Archon: Morax (Rex Lapis, Zhongli), oldest of The Seven. Nation: Liyue, now governed by humans.

Morax was born more than six thousand years ago and became Archon by winning the Archon War in the region. After faking his death in the Rite of Descension, he arranged a test of whether Liyue could manage without him, with the help of the Tsaritsa and her Fatui, and retired. He now works as a consultant at the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor under Hu Tao. Few know he is the Archon. Along with Barbatos he is one of the two original members of The Seven who remain.

Gnosis and authority: After the Rite of Parting in Archon Quest Chapter I, Act III (1.0), Signora, as the Tsaritsa's envoy, collected the Geo Gnosis from Zhongli peacefully under the contract he called the "contract to end all contracts". The Tsaritsa's end of the bargain is still unexplained.

Elemental beings: Azhdaha, the Geo Dragon Sovereign, sealed beneath the Dragon-Queller; Geo elemental lifeforms such as Geo Slimes, Geo Specters and the Geo Hypostasis; and the Geovishap line of dragons.

Azhdaha was a friend of Morax whom Morax once gave sight, and who suffered from erosion until he lashed out at people. He was sealed in the Chasm and beneath the Dragon-Queller at Nantianmen. Geo Slimes are small and drifting, Geo Specters float and burst into earthquake-like attacks, and the Geo Hypostasis (code name Gimel) is a boss in the Guyun Stone Forest with a high-density solid shell around a reactive core. It raises pillars and drops them as stone seals.

Known uses: Barriers and shields, summoned stone constructs, pillars of rock, shaking the ground, and petrifying or fixing a target in place.

Geo shapes land as well as fights. Morax is said to have raised mountains, lowered tides and bound a sea god with stone lances. Geo Vision holders in play raise constructs and crystalline shields.

Limits: Geo does not react with Anemo or Dendro; it crystallises Pyro, Hydro, Electro and Cryo.

Crystallize turns Pyro, Hydro, Electro or Cryo into a shard of that element that grants a shield when picked up; it does not create an element.

Interactions: Crystallize: Geo meeting Pyro, Hydro, Electro or Cryo makes an elemental shard whose pickup gives a shield (own entry). Geo also gives Shatter, in which hitting a frozen target deals Physical damage and ends the freeze.

Lunar-Crystallize (Geo plus Hydro, 6.3): creates three Moondrifts near the target, Geo constructs that resonate after enough Lunar-Crystallize reactions, firing Moondrift Harmony for Geo damage.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): Geo is a damage type and the element of characters such as Zhongli, Ningguang, Albedo, Noelle, Gorou, Yun Jin, Arataki Itto, Navia, Chiori, Xilonen, Kachina, Zibai, Illuga and Linnea, plus the Geo Traveler. Geoculi are scattered across Liyue.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): show Geo as weight, stillness and pattern: amber-gold light, hexagonal or crystal facets, dust settling, a faint hum in stone. It protects more often than it strikes; a Geo defender plants themselves, and a shield that appears should read as solid, not glowing energy. Keep scale proportionate: a Vision holder can raise a pillar or a crystalline barrier, but reshaping mountains and binding a god is an Archon's work.

104.content: The Geo Archon is Morax, called Rex Lapis in Liyue and by many other titles. He faked his death during the Rite of Descension and gave his Gnosis to the Tsaritsa, leaving Liyue to humans. He lives as Zhongli, a funeral-parlor consultant in Liyue Harbor. His own character entry carries his biography, so this entry only points at the element.

105.content: Azhdaha is the Geo Dragon Sovereign, an ancient Geovishap ancestor who once ruled a territory including what is now Liyue. Morax stopped the earthquakes that his movements caused, gave him sight, and made a contract with him. Erosion and human mining in the Chasm eventually drove him to attack the people he had loved, and he was sealed under the Dragon-Queller at Nantianmen. He is incapacitated, not dead, as of Amidst Chaos, the Rock Is Unmoved.

106.content: Geoculi are found scattered across Liyue. The item text calls a Geoculus a substance that has accumulated intense Geo energy, to be offered at a Statue of The Seven to reinstate power it has lost over the years. In gameplay there are 131 in the overworld.

107.content: When Geo meets Pyro, Hydro, Electro or Cryo, Crystallize leaves a shard of that element on the ground. Picking it up gives the character a shield of that element. Shards last 15 seconds and only the three newest remain. Lunar-Crystallize is the Hydro version introduced in 6.3. Crystallize is a gameplay mechanic with only metaphorical support in lore.

108.content:
Hexerei (also: Hexerei: Secret Rite, Hexerei character, Hexerei characters, Witch's Eve Rite): Hexerei (German for witchcraft) is a party Team Bonus introduced in Version 6.2. Certain characters become "Hexerei characters" by completing their Witch's Homework quests. Bring two or more into the party and the bonus Hexerei: Secret Rite activates, strengthening them.

The system is built around the Hexenzirkel's "homework" for the Traveler. The Hexerei characters at launch were Sucrose, Mona, Durin, Klee, Albedo, Venti, Fischl and Razor; Varka, Nicole, Lohen and Prune were added later.

In universe: In the fiction, the Witch's Homework is set by witches. In the quest Unexpected Commission, Lisa of the Knights of Favonius library and the mage Alice have the Traveler sort a huge anonymous donation of books, among them banned ones, and the Traveler receives The Little Witch's Dictionary. Its description says it was made by the witches and "claims to explain" the storybook The Little Witch and the Undying Fire, while really containing homework tailored by the Hexenzirkel for each reader.

Gameplay: Gameplay: finishing a character's Witch's Homework makes them a Hexerei character. With at least two Hexerei characters in the party, Hexerei: Secret Rite is active.

Requirements: complete the Prologue Archon Quest Act III, finish Witch's Homework: Solution (the quest begins in Mondstadt City) to receive The Little Witch's Dictionary, own the character and have them at level 70 or higher. Each character then has their own homework quest.
In Witch's Homework: Solution, the Traveler may also invite one of Fischl, Sucrose or Razor to the party; only one can be chosen.
The Secret Rite gives each Hexerei character their Witch's Eve Rite Passive, an additional talent, and enhances some of their other talents and Constellations. Most of those effects work only while two or more Hexerei characters are in the party. Two weapons, Athame Artis and The Daybreak Chronicles, show their own effects when the party has the bonus.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): treat "Hexerei" as a loose bond of witch-adjacent people drawn together by the Traveler's homework, not a formal guild. A scene with two or more Hexerei characters can feel charged or unusually in tune, but avoid giving them powers beyond their own.

109.content: The Witch's Eve Rite Passive is an additional talent unlocked for a character once they finish their Witch's Homework. It is part of Hexerei: Secret Rite and enhances other talents and Constellations of that character.

110.content: A gadget received from Alice in the quest Unexpected Commission. It lists and starts the Witch's Homework quests. Its description says the witches made it and that it is "actually filled with homework tailored by the Hexenzirkel."

111.content:
Hydro (also: Hydro element, element of water): Hydro is the element of water, one of Teyvat's seven elements. Its homeland is Fontaine, the nation of justice. Two gods held the title of Hydro Archon, Egeria and then Focalors. Focalors executed herself in 4.2 and destroyed the Hydro Archon's divine throne, so Fontaine has had no Hydro Archon since. The Hydro Authority now belongs to Neuvillette, the reborn Hydro Dragon Sovereign.

Hydro ascension gems are Varunada Lazurite. Hydro users appear well beyond Fontaine; the Fatui Harbinger Tartaglia and Columbina of Nod-Krai both wield Hydro.

In universe: Most people use Hydro through a Vision. Neuvillette needs none, because the Hydro Authority is his own. In how it interacts with other elements, rain, rivers, the sea and the Primordial Sea beneath Fontaine all count as Hydro.

Fontaine was where the old Hydro Dragon ruled the Primordial Sea; Hydro vishap legend calls the Dragon its "beating heart". After the Dragon fell, Egeria became the god of Fontaine and gave it its laws. Hydro in Fontaine is entwined with justice, trials and the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale.

Archon and nation: Hydro Archon: none as of 7.1. The divine throne was destroyed in 4.2. The two former Archons were Egeria and Focalors, both Gods of Justice among The Seven. Nation: Fontaine.

Egeria presided over Fontaine from about 2,000 to 500 years ago, after the fall of Remuria, uniting the surviving tribes and establishing its laws. She died in battle at Tunigi Hollow during the Cataclysm and her body became the waters of the Amrita. Focalors, originally an Oceanid familiar of Egeria, succeeded her and governed for 499 years.

Gnosis and authority: The Hydro Gnosis powered the Oratrice, which was secretly merged with Focalors; only a little of the Indemnitium gathered from trials at the Opera Epiclese ran the Court, and the rest was stored so she could execute herself. When Focalors died the Oratrice stopped working, but the Hydro Gnosis was unaffected. Archons keep their divine thrones and elemental power whether or not they hold their Gnosis.

Elemental beings: Hydro Slimes, Hydro Samachurls, Hydro Specters, Hydro Mimics (summoned by Oceanids) and the Hydro Hypostasis. The Hydro Dragon Sovereign is Neuvillette.

Oceanids, occasionally called the Lochfolk, are beings of pure Hydro energy from Fontaine who float through the air, command water and make Hydro Mimics, water creatures that copy animals. Hydro Slimes form from Hydro dispersed through nature; legend says travellers once packed them as emergency water, though the dense Hydro makes drinking one harmful. Hydro Samachurls are aged hilichurl shamans who chant to the power of Hydro and call rain that heals allies.

Known uses: Currents, jets, bubbles, rain and tides, healing water, and soaking things so that they react to Electro and Cryo.

Neuvillette commands the Primordial Sea's waters and can draw out the memories stored in water. Hydro Samachurls heal allies with rain.

Limits: Hydro alone only soaks; it needs another element to do something special.

Wet itself has no special effect; it only allows Hydro reactions. A Vision fixes its holder to one element, while Archons and Sovereigns hold an Authority rather than a Vision.

Interactions: Hydro reacts with Pyro (Vaporize), Cryo (Frozen), Electro (Electro-Charged), Anemo (Swirl), Geo (Crystallize) and Dendro (Bloom).

Bloom extends to Hyperbloom (Electro on a Dendro Core) and Burgeon (Pyro on a Dendro Core). Lunar reactions add Lunar-Charged (Hydro with Electro), Lunar-Bloom (Hydro with Dendro) and Lunar-Crystallize (Hydro with Geo).

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): Hydro is a damage type and the element of characters such as Neuvillette, Furina, Sigewinne, Tartaglia, Columbina, Vodyanitsa (added in 7.1) and the Hydro Traveler.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): show Hydro as flow, weight and sound: drips, condensation on glass, spray, a hush before rain. Blue and pale teal are safe visual cues. Keep scale proportionate: a Vision holder can raise a jet, bubble or wave; moving the sea is a Sovereign's work.

112.content: Two gods held the Hydro Archon title: Egeria, the Mistress of Many Waters, and Focalors, the Regina of All Waters, Kindreds, Peoples and Laws. Focalors's death in 4.2 destroyed the divine throne, so as of 7.1 no Hydro Archon exists.

113.content: The Hydro Dragon Sovereign was the old ruler of water and the vishaps, one of the Seven Sovereigns. It died in the war against the Heavenly Principles and was reborn in human form as Neuvillette, who regained its Authority in 4.2.

114.content: Hydroculi are collectible substances of intense Hydro energy found across Fontaine and the Sea of Bygone Eras. Offered at a Statue of The Seven, they help restore power the statue has lost over the years. There are 271 in total.

115.content: Varunada Lazurites are the ascension gems for Hydro characters. The gemstone's description quotes an unnamed speaker on ideals without stain and on laws and the Tribunal being able to judge even the speaker; the wiki reads the lines as fitting the 4.2 Archon Quest and the Oratrice's sentence on Focalors.

116.content: Oceanids are beings of pure Hydro from Fontaine who followed Egeria. Legend says her first tear created the first Oceanid. She gave some of them human forms with water from the Primordial Sea, which the Heavenly Principles counted as a sin, and many Oceanids left Fontaine after her death.

117.content:
Hyperbloom (also: Hyperbloom reaction, Electro Bloom reaction, Sprawling Shot): Hyperbloom is a Dendro elemental reaction. When Electro touches a Dendro Core (the orb a Bloom leaves behind), the core becomes a homing projectile, a Sprawling Shot, which flies to the closest enemy and bursts in a small area for strong Dendro damage. It is the Electro counterpart of Burgeon.

It debuted in Version 3.0 with Bloom, Burgeon, Quicken, Spread and Aggravate, the reactions introduced for Dendro. A Bloom, from Dendro and Hydro, has to make the core first.

In universe: Canon gives no in-world explanation for Hyperbloom. The pages read treat it only as a combat rule, so it is best understood as a charged seed of plant energy flung at a foe.

Gameplay: Gameplay: when Electro is applied to a Dendro Core, Hyperbloom triggers. The core turns into a Sprawling Shot that homes in on the nearest enemy and deals Dendro area damage on impact.

- The shot hits in a small radius of 1 m, compared with the 5 m burst of Burgeon, and the wiki lists it with increased damage over an ordinary Bloom core.
- If an enemy or the environment triggers it, the shot homes in on the closest ally instead. The wiki adds that the Lea Lotus Lamp made by the Dendro Traveler's Elemental Burst counts as a target for Hyperbloom in that case.
- The damage hits enemies and players alike; damage to players from Bloom-related reactions is 2% of the damage to enemies.
- It can be triggered by a party other than the one that made the Bloom, including the environment, and its damage scales with the party that applied the Electro.
- Hyperbloom is a transformative reaction: it does its own damage, based on the triggering character's level and Elemental Mastery, and ignores ATK and cannot critically strike unless a talent or constellation allows it.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): show a green, lumpy seed of energy hanging in the air, a crackle of lightning touching it, and the seed lunging away in a streak of sparking vines to strike a target. Keep it quick and precise rather than a huge blast.

Limits: Hyperbloom needs a Dendro Core, so it needs Bloom first. It does nothing to a Bountiful Core.

The shot can hurt the party too, though far less than it hurts enemies. The core vanishes after its duration if its creator has left the party.

Examples: Gameplay example: Hydro and Dendro together leave a Dendro Core. An Electro attack on it triggers Hyperbloom at once and a Sprawling Shot homes in on the nearest enemy.

118.content: The Sprawling Shot is the homing projectile that a Dendro Core becomes when Electro triggers Hyperbloom. It deals Dendro area damage in a small radius on impact and seeks the nearest enemy, or ally if an enemy or the environment set it off.

119.content: A Dendro Core is what the Bloom reaction (Dendro with Hydro) leaves behind. If left alone it bursts after about six seconds. Pyro on it triggers Burgeon, Electro triggers Hyperbloom. No more than five can exist at a time.

120.content:
Immortality and Resurrection (also: curse of immortality, Curse of Immortality, immortality in Teyvat, resurrection in Teyvat, Curse of Death, Elixir of Immortality): Teyvat has no single rule for avoiding death. Canon shows separate, bounded cases: the Curse of Immortality that Ronova, Ruler of Death, laid on pure-blooded Khaenri'ahns 500 years ago; long-lived adepti, gods and dragons, who still die or erode; zombies such as Qiqi; and Natlan's conditional Ode of Resurrection.

Each case has a cost: the curse stops dying and ageing but not mental and spiritual decay; zombies lose memory or feeling; the Ode needs a victory and heals only fatal wounds. The Authorities of Life and Death, held by two of the Four Shades, are what Celestia polices.

In universe: - Cursed immortality: pure-blooded Khaenri'ahns, by Ronova.
- Longevity: adepti, gods and dragons live for millennia but can die or be worn away.
- Zombification: adeptal energy (Qiqi) or an Elixir of Immortality (Jialiang).
- Resurrection: Natlan's Ode, for fallen Ancient Name bearers.

Ordinary people age and die; no source gives a human lifespan.

Curse of immortality: During the Cataclysm 500 years ago, Ronova cursed Khaenri'ah's pure-blooded people with immortality as a punishment. They cannot die or age, but they still erode. Khaenri'ahns of mixed or foreign descent were instead turned into monsters, per the wiki's reading of the story.

Erosion and the curse: Dainsleif says the curse denies death but does not promise that those under it will never die: body and soul keep eroding until they are nearly nonexistent, even if death is not the form that erosion takes. His ring, a gift from his brother Vedrfolnir, continually resets his body's condition and lets him keep his memories better than other Khaenri'ahns, though his mind still erodes.

Zombies: A zombie is a person brought back from death, usually cold and stiff, with talismans to hold the state. Qiqi was never awakened by anyone and gives herself orders. She has poor memory, little expression, no sense of smell, prefers cold, and her flesh decays in heat. Jialiang, revived by Baizhu's Elixir of Immortality, is the only other known zombie.

Adepti and longevity: The adepti are very long-lived but not immortal. Liyue still holds the Rite of Parting, a memorial service run by Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, for each adeptus who passes, though it has been needed only a handful of times in three thousand years.

Ode of resurrection: In Natlan the Ode of Resurrection, a ceremony at the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, raises Ancient Name bearers who died fighting the Abyss in the Night Warden Wars, provided their group achieved victory. The Pyro Archon enters the Sacred Flame to seek the deceased and their name in the Night Kingdom while the crowd sings. It heals fatal injuries only, and its power comes from Ronova.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): fallen party members can be revived at a Statue of The Seven or with a dish. No story source treats these as literal in-world resurrection.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): treat any return from death as costly and conditional. A Khaenri'ahn survivor should feel tired, not triumphant; a zombie should show cold, stiffness or forgetfulness; an adeptus's death is a rare, formal event.

Limits: No source describes a way to undo the Curse of Immortality, and no resurrection is unconditional.

Ronova could not simply break her own rules (Capitano's paradox), and when she exceeded the limits Celestia permitted, it reclaimed her Authority. The Ode needs victory, a name, a fatal wound and a Pyro Archon willing to enter the flame.

121.comment: Immortality and Resurrection: Curse of Immortality
121.content: Ronova, the Ruler of Death, cursed the pure-blooded Khaenri'ahns with immortality during the Cataclysm 500 years ago. They cannot die or age but are not shielded from erosion, which gradually dissolves memory, will and spirit. Dainsleif and Capitano are among the cursed. As of 7.1, Ronova's Authority is reclaimed, but the characters who live with the curse still treat it as active.

122.content:
Karma (also: karmic debt, divine karma, bad karma, karma of the yakshas): Karma, or karmic debt, is the corruptive residue left by the wills and powers of ancient gods slain in the Archon War. It seeps into land, monsters and people, and can drive humans mad. The yakshas were called by Rex Lapis to destroy it, and absorbed so much of it that most died or went insane. As of 7.1 the sole surviving yaksha, Xiao, still bears it.

The term is used mainly in Liyue. Adepti can make a medicine that temporarily eases karma, but like most adeptal medicines it is lethal to mortals.

In universe: During the Archon War, Morax subdued many gods. Their hatred and powers lingered in the world as half-awake remnants that corrupted land, spawned monsters and caused pestilence, miasma and mutations. Contact with karma can make humans insane and makes monsters stronger.

Morax summoned the yakshas, especially fierce illuminated beasts, to fight these remnants. As Zhongli narrates in the cinematic of Glimmers of the Vigilant Yaksha, they swore to restore order through slaughter, but each kill left a mark: the debt wore into their souls, and they went mad with fear, turned on each other or were lost to the darkness. Of the five foremost yakshas, three died and Bosacius vanished, leaving Xiao as the only one.

Effects and resistance: Karma corrupts monsters and strengthens them, and can send humans insane. Yelan's clan story adds that her ancestor found temporary relief from his insanity only near the Wangshu Inn. Vision holders have heightened resistance, as do the Traveler and illuminated beasts; in the adepti's view, a Vision is a valid form of illumination.

Relief and remedies: Remedies are partial. Adepti alchemy yields Remedium Tertiorum, which Zhongli once asked a traveler to pass to Xiao, but it can be lethal to mortals. Venti once relieved Xiao's pain by playing the flute through the night, which Xiao's profile describes as quieting his wild senses; the Liyue legend of the sound of a flute among the reeds near Dihua Marsh is tied to this. The Qixing built Wangshu Inn at Dihua Marsh to give Xiao a place to rest, and he eats Almond Tofu there.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, Xiao remains the last yaksha and still carries the karmic debt. No release up to the cutoff resolves or removes karma, and no canon source says it has been cured.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): karma appears in Xiao's character materials and quests such as The Purging of Evil, the Karma-Heavy Cavern domain, and the idle quotes of Xiao as a companion, one of which is simply "Karma..." There is no general karma mechanic in the open world.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): treat karma as a heavy, quiet burden rather than a spell. Xiao keeps people away, speaks little of it and does not ask for pity; the yaksha's own line in the profile says yakshas need no sympathy or tears. Show it through weariness, sudden pain, cold sweat or a distant, haunted look, not melodrama.

123.content: The yakshas were fierce illuminated beasts summoned by Morax to destroy the lingering hatred of defeated gods. Five stood foremost: Bosacius the eldest and leader, Indarias, Bonanus, Menogias and Alatus (Xiao). Accumulated karma destroyed them. Bonanus, Indarias and Menogias died, Bosacius went mad and vanished, and Alatus alone remains.

124.content: An adeptal medicine that Zhongli gave to the Traveler to pass to Xiao. It can temporarily ease karma, but nothing in the world can withstand its power, and like other adeptal medicines it is lethal to mortals, so he warned that Paimon must not eat them.

125.content: An inn at Dihua Marsh built at least five hundred years ago by the Liyue Qixing to give Xiao somewhere to stay and rest while he does his duty. It is run by Qixing agents Verr Goldet and Huai'an.

126.content:
Khvarena (also: Spirit Light, Khvarena of flowers, the Khvarena, Great Khvarena): Khvarena is a pure, divine energy of Sumeru. Nabu Malikata, the Goddess of Flowers, made it for one purpose: to oppose the cataclysm she foresaw. Its divine nature lets it purify Abyssal energy and Forbidden Knowledge. She called the first Khvarena her innocent, pure daughter and gave it to Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, who shaped it into the divine bird Simurgh. When the Abyss began to corrupt the Amrita, Simurgh shattered her form into countless motes of Khvarena. The only sentient ones became the Pari.

The name is a Zoroastrian term for divine glory or radiance, and game texts use the word loosely: for the original being (spoken of as feminine), for the countless entities she became when she divided, and for the abstract quality of light and favour ("do not let your Khvarena dim"). Related Sumeru items include the Vourukasha's Glow artifact set and the Great Songs of Khvarena.

In universe: Khvarena is not presented as an element and is not tied to a Vision. It is an energy of divine life and purity, opposed to the darkness of the Abyss. It exists in many forms: wild motes in the Girdle of the Sands, the Pari, Plumes of Purifying Light and orbs of coalesced light that can raise barriers.

The origin is told in two ways. A legend relayed by Sethos says Rukkhadevata received the Khvarena as a gift at the first Sabzeruz Festival. The artifact texts of Vourukasha's Glow instead show Nabu Malikata handing over a shard of her own being, after a dream of a faceless nightmare (the cataclysm), asking Rukkhadevata to keep it safe until the day the Abyss rises to drown life. Both agree on the purpose: to blunt a disaster that Nabu foresaw.

Origins: Nabu Malikata, one of the three companion-gods of the old desert kingdom, foresaw the cataclysm. She separated a piece of her own being, called it her innocent and pure daughter, and gave it to her friend Greater Lord Rukkhadevata to protect and to use against the coming darkness. After Nabu and King Deshret died, Rukkhadevata, per the artifact texts, turned the Khvarena into a divine bird.

Simurgh and the pari: When the cataclysm came, the Amrita (made from the remains of Egeria, the earlier Hydro Archon, slain in the upheaval) began to be corrupted by the Abyss. To save it, Simurgh flew into the pool and shattered her form, becoming countless motes of Khvarena. These formed the Vourukasha Oasis, a sea of flowers. The only motes with intelligence became the Pari, who consider their god to be Egeria, whose consciousness lies in the Harvisptokhm.

Great songs: Zurvan says that, in the past, she used the Khvarena to repair the seal that held back the darkness and fused the strongest Khvarena into five Great Songs to purify the land. Item and tutorial text describe them as the physical form of Khvarena's might, which create barriers; only a Pari with the Twin-Horned Chaplet, the symbol of Khvarena's recognition, can touch them. Sorush, who is given the Chaplet, goes with the Traveler to collect them.

Known uses: Purifying: cleansing Abyssal energy and Forbidden Knowledge, and repairing seals against the Abyss. Raising barriers. Giving life to the Vourukasha Oasis.

In Sorush's hands, orbs of coalesced Khvarena in the desert can be woken to expand a barrier that deflects incoming attacks. Pari can use their link to Khvarena to guide its power. Plumes of Purifying Light can be offered to the Amrita Pool.

Limits: Khvarena is not unlimited. Its sentient form, the Pari, lives out a fated duty and ends as a plume; the great form, Simurgh, gave up her shape. It cannot cleanse every taint: a Pari that is corrupted is rejected by the Oasis and becomes a tree.

Only a Pari with the Chaplet can handle the Great Songs. Their effect, in the quest, did not extend to things not tied to the Abyss. Canon shows no ordinary person wielding Khvarena as a power.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): Khvarena appears as exploration content in the Girdle of the Sands, including Khvarena Mayflies, Khvarena Barrier orbs, Plumes of Purifying Light and Great Songs, all tied to Sorush's gadget and the Khvarena of Good and Evil quests. The artifact set Vourukasha's Glow carries its lore in item texts.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): portray Khvarena as soft, clean light, the feel of petals, dew and clear water, not as a weapon. Pari speak of it as a sacred inheritance and a duty.

127.content: Simurgh was the divine bird made when Greater Lord Rukkhadevata gave a shape to the Khvarena that Nabu Malikata had entrusted to her. She slept until the cataclysm, then shattered her form in the Amrita Pool to purify it, becoming countless motes of Khvarena. The Pari descend from her. See her own entry for details.

128.content: The Pari are avian, flower-like descendants of Simurgh who live in the Vourukasha Oasis in the Girdle of the Sands. They are the only sentient form of Khvarena, each with a fated duty. When their life ends they become Plumes of Purifying Light, to be returned to the Amrita Pool. Tainted Pari turn into Fravashi Trees. Humans bonded with Pari are called Yasnapati.

129.content: Five concentrated forms of Khvarena, fused by Zurvan from the strongest Khvarena collected in the flower sea to purify the land. Only a Pari carrying the Twin-Horned Chaplet can touch them. In the Khvarena of Good and Evil quests, Sorush and the Traveler gather them; Nasejuna, with the Abyss Order, tries to seize them.

130.content:
Kresnik Kristall (also: Kristall, Kresnik's Torch, Kresnik Torch, Kresnik Energy): Kresnik Kristall is the crystalline ore that keeps Snezhnaya warm. Burned in furnaces called Kresnik's Torches, it gives off heat efficiently, and every Snezhnayan city is built around one such torch. The ore is mined chiefly in Novokitezhgrad and shipped across the nation by rail.

The Royal Energy Commission of Snezhnaya oversees both the torches and the Kristall's transport and use. In gameplay the Eye of Graeae turns Kresnik Energy from Kristall and torches into protection against the cold.

In universe: Most Snezhnayan settlements need Kresnik Kristall to survive. Before the torches existed, the Eye of Graeae says, the land was made only of Frigid and Subzero Zones and unfit for human life.

A torch holds a Normal Temperature Zone within a certain range and shields a city from snowstorms. Small civilian-model torches also stand across the countryside. Villages without a rail stop depend on deliveries; in "Gunfire in the Silent Lands" a character from the village of Alatyr fears that if Kristall deliveries have stopped there, the villagers will freeze.

Origin: The Kristall is said to come from power released when the Cryo Dragon Sovereign lost control in Snezhnaya. A potion formula found in a world quest calls the ore the ideal material, as power refined from the authority released by a colossal beast of ages past that lost control.

Known uses: Burned in a Kresnik's Torch, Kristall provides heat. Gameplay (not literal lore): each ore deposit and many torches release Kresnik Energy that the Eye of Graeae uses to keep the Traveler from Sheer Cold.

Limits: Do not treat the ore as a source of elemental power for combat or as Cryo itself; canon describes its use as heat and energy for survival. Do not claim a character can make Kristall by Cryo or Pyro power.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): in Snezhnaya, warmth is a civic fact. Characters notice how far a torch reaches, speak of stove-fuel and coal-like shipments, and feel a rail delay as a danger rather than an inconvenience. Foreigners are surprised that a Snezhnayan town is built around a heat source.

131.content: A furnace that burns Kresnik Kristall for heat. Large torches anchor cities, small civilian ones stand across the land, and the most important sits in Kresnik's Burning Heart beneath Snezhnograd. Prototype torches remain at the Pale Crown Palace. The Royal Energy Commission maintains them.

132.comment: Kresnik Kristall: Royal Energy Commission of Snezhnaya
132.content: The Commission, seated in Snezhnograd, maintains the torches and manages the transport and use of the Kristall. Its acting chair is Zarechnaya; members include Mitya, Yelagina and Zaretsky. Its history is not documented in canon read here.

133.content: A beetle found near Snezhnayan mines whose shell resembles the ore. Local lore says people first found the deposits by following these bugs' trails.

134.content:
Lunar-Bloom (also: Lunar Bloom, Lunar-Bloom reaction, Verdant Dew): Lunar-Bloom is the Lunar Reaction between Dendro and Hydro, in either order. When the party includes a character whose Moonsign Benediction passive enables it, ordinary Bloom is replaced by Lunar-Bloom. By itself it does no damage. Instead it gives the party Verdant Dew, a stored resource certain characters spend to deal Lunar-Bloom damage, which can crit. It arrived in Version 6.0 (Luna I) with Nod-Krai.

The Dendro Cores and Bountiful Cores that the reaction still creates are identical to those from Bloom. Damage from those cores is not counted as Lunar-Bloom damage.

In universe: Canon offers no in-world explanation. Verdant Dew and Lunar-Bloom are shown in tutorials and combat, not discussed by characters in the sources read. Treat them as a gameplay abstraction.

Related setting: the reaction came with the Nod-Krai region and the Moonsign party bonus. It replaces Bloom, the Dendro and Hydro reaction from Version 3.0.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): Lunar-Bloom does no damage on its own. The only ways to deal Lunar-Bloom damage are certain character talents and constellations, which spend Verdant Dew.

- After Lunar-Bloom triggers, the party gains 1 Verdant Dew every 2.5 seconds for 2.5 seconds. The party can hold up to 3.
- Triggering Lunar-Bloom again while dew is being gained resets the duration.
- Verdant Dew lasts indefinitely. It persists through party changes, teleports between maps and domains, daily resets and game sessions.
